Question: In a tournament there are six teams that play each other twice. A team earns \(3\) points for a win, \(1\) point for a draw, and \(0\) points for a loss. After all the games have been played it turns out that the top three teams earned the same number of total points. What is the greatest possible number of total points for each of the top three teams?
Solution:
First bound the combined score of the top three teams. A game awards at most \(3\) total points: a win and loss award \(3+0\), while a draw awards only \(1+1=2\).

Among the top three teams there are three pairs, each playing twice, for \(6\) games. These contribute at most \(6\cdot3=18\) points to their combined score. Against the bottom three teams, each top team plays \(3\cdot2=6\) games. That is \(18\) games altogether, worth at most \(18\cdot3=54\) points to the top teams.

Their combined score is at most \(18+54=72\). Since their scores are equal, each has at most \(72/3=24\) points.

This bound can be reached. Let every top team win all six games against the bottom teams, earning \(18\) points. Between each pair of top teams, let each win one game. Each top team then has two more wins and two losses, earning another \(6\) points. All three finish with \(24\), while every bottom team can earn at most \(12\) from its games against the other bottom teams.

Thus they really are the top three, and the maximum is \(\boxed{24}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). A maximum argument needs both an upper bound and a schedule that attains it.
